sectors.name: Electronics manufacturing

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: Kotak expected EMS coverage revenue to grow 21% YoY in Q1 FY27 on consumer and industrial demand, with Mobile PLI 2.0 and ISM 2.0 proposed.
MOFSL's EMS coverage grew Q2 FY27 sales 49% and PAT 29% YoY.
risks: Margins are under pressure as topline growth is partly offset by costs (Kotak).
MOFSL's Aug-2026 snapshot puts the sector at ~94x FY26 earnings, pricing in its 36%/60% EPS growth forecasts.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (EMS EPS growth 35.8% FY27E, 60.0% FY28E); Kotak Institutional Equities EMS preview (10-07-2026)

sectors.why: It has the fastest forecast earnings growth of any sector, but valuations near 70-95x leave no room for execution misses.

sectors.name: Retail

returns.basis: index (total return); Nifty India Consumption is a broad consumption proxy, not pure retail
returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (organised apparel retail revenue, 1-year)
tailwinds: Crisil expects organised apparel retail revenue to grow 12-13% in FY27, led by value fashion and expansion beyond big cities.
Crisil expects organised jewellery retail revenue to rise 20-25% in FY27 on higher gold prices.
risks: Apparel growth was only high single digits in April-August 2026 (Crisil), so the festive season is critical.
Jewellery volumes are projected to fall 13-15% in FY27 (Crisil).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Retail EPS growth 34.5% FY27E, 28.3% FY28E); Crisil Ratings apparel retail (10-09-2026) and jewellery retail reports (2026)

valuation.source: Trailing P/E: NSE Indices published figure via marketcalls.in (20-11-2026); long-run median 39.03 since 2011. pe5yAvg: Trendlyne '5 Years PE Range' average for the same index, read 20-11-2026.

sectors.why: Listed retailers are compounding profits above 30%, but the consumption proxy index has fallen ~10% in a year.

sectors.name: Textiles and apparel

business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Textile (8 companies); sector not tabulated in Q3/Q4 FY26

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (apparel export revenue, 1-year)
tailwinds: ICRA expects apparel export revenue to rebound 8-11% in FY27 after the US cut tariffs to 18% from 25%.
Crisil sees cotton-yarn revenue rising 9-11% in FY27, with export revenue up 12-14%.
risks: Apparel exports fell 11.25% YoY in June 2026 even as textile exports rose (CITI).
FY26 textile and apparel exports grew only ~2% (Ministry of Textiles), showing demand is fragile.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Textiles EPS growth 53.1% FY27E, 24.5% FY28E); ICRA apparel sector (Feb/Mar-2026); Crisil Ratings cotton yarn (2026)

sectors.why: The US tariff cut sets up an FY27 export rebound from a depressed base, but monthly export data is still uneven.

sectors.name: Agriculture and agri inputs

returns.basis: index (total return); covers only the sugar and ethanol sub-sector
returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

tailwinds: DAM Capital expects tight supply through FY27, with opening sugar stocks at a decade-low 3 million tonnes, keeping prices elevated.
Ethanol blending held at ~20% in ESY2026 (ICRA).
risks: Crisil expects sugar-mill margins to fall 140-160 bp to ~6% in FY27 as ethanol diversion shrinks and cane costs rise.
Crisil sees gross sugar output easing to about 29 million tonnes in SS2027, and El Nino threatens yields.
outlook.source: Crisil Ratings sugar report (09-11-2026); DAM Capital (31-08-2026); ICRA sugar updates (2026)

valuation.source: Trailing P/E: NSE Indices published figure via marketcalls.in (20-11-2026); long-run median 26.11 since 2026.

sectors.why: Firm sugar prices are offset by an ethanol-margin squeeze, leaving earnings under pressure in FY27.

sectors.name: Logistics and transport

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: ICRA's logistics sample grew revenue 16.8% YoY in Q1 FY27 on higher freight rates.
Emkay expects Delhivery to lead Q2 FY27 logistics growth at ~20% YoY.
risks: ICRA expects road-logistics growth to come mainly from freight rates, with soft volumes.
Fuel costs could squeeze road-logistics margins by up to 200 bp in FY27 (ICRA).

valuation.source: Trailing P/E: NSE Indices published figure via marketcalls.in (20-11-2026); long-run median 35.08 since 2022.

sectors.why: Revenue growth of 8-10% is price-led and the index trades well above its median at 42x.

sectors.name: Aviation

tailwinds: ICRA still expects domestic passenger traffic to grow 3-6% in FY27.
Passenger load factors improved meaningfully in June 2026 (ICRA).
risks: ICRA expects an industry net loss of Rs 360-380 billion in FY27 on high ATF prices and a weak rupee.
Domestic traffic fell 6.3% YoY in August 2026 (ICRA).

sectors.why: Losses are widening on fuel and currency, and traffic is falling year on year.

sectors.name: Hospitality and tourism

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Travel & Leisure (3 companies); sector not tabulated in Q3/Q4 FY26

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (hotel industry revenue, 1-year)
tailwinds: ICRA projects hospitality revenue up 7-9% in FY27 after 11% in FY26, on leisure, MICE and wedding demand.
Premium hotel occupancy is seen at 72-74% with room rates of Rs 8,600-8,800 in FY27 (ICRA).
risks: The West Asia conflict weighs on inbound and transit travellers (ICRA).
The index trades at 87x trailing earnings, at its 93rd percentile.

Industry ARPU rose at an 11% CAGR from Rs 142 in FY23 to Rs 196 in FY26 (CareEdge).
risks: Subscriber growth has slowed to 3-4% a year, so growth depends on tariff hikes (CareEdge).
A delayed or smaller tariff hike would cut the FY27 ARPU uplift.

sectors.why: The listed education universe is small and fragmented, and no sector-level earnings or demand data was found.

sectors.name: Paper and packaging

tailwinds: ICRA says packaging drives the paper industry's growth on ~20% volume growth from capacity additions and e-commerce, FMCG and pharma demand.
Crisil expects jute volumes up ~15% in FY27, with margins widening 130 bp.
risks: The printing and writing paper segment underperforms on intense competition and weak realisations (ICRA).
Packaging firms face raw-material volatility from the West Asia crisis.
outlook.source: ICRA Indian Paper Manufacturing Industry (Dec-2025); Crisil Ratings jute (Sep-2026)

sectors.why: Packaging-led volume growth is offset by weak realisations in writing and printing paper.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Staffing (4 companies), the closest MOFSL proxy for industrial services

tailwinds: The FY27 Union Budget raised infrastructure spending 11% to Rs 12.2 trillion, which supports consultancy and project-management demand.
MOFSL's staffing coverage grew Q2 FY27 PAT 34% YoY on 15% sales growth.
risks: Consultancy order flow depends on public capex timing.
Staffing margins are thin and wage-cost driven.
